# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, ready. I feel 5 wire positions but no other info. Waiting for instructions from the manual.

I need to figure out how to communicate with Deaf and Blind despite my constraints. I can't speak at all, only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. Blind cannot see gestures or hear speech from me at all - I have no way to reach Blind directly!

Let me reconsider the chain: Blind speaks → Mute and Deaf hear it. Mute (me) gestures → only Deaf sees it. Deaf speaks → Blind and Mute hear it.

So the only path from me to Blind is: Mute → gesture → Deaf → speak → Blind. I need to encode my manual info into gestures that Deaf can relay verbally to Blind.

I need a gesture code for light colors and wire colors. Let me establish a simple mapping using distinct gesture symbols, then explain the mapping so Deaf can translate to words for Blind.

Since Deaf needs to see the bomb's light color, they'll know which light is lit. I need to give Deaf the full mapping table via gestures, using one symbol per color, consistently.

Let me assign:
- blue = 👍
- green = 👎
- red = 👌
- white = ☝
- yellow = ✌

Table: blue→blue, green→white, red→yellow, white→red, yellow→green

I'll send pairs: light-color gesture then cut-color gesture, five times, in fixed order so Deaf can parse it.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | white |
| red | yellow |
| white | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is blue. Wires in order: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue.
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: Display shows 0, Light is blue. Wires in order: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Waiting for your instructions on what to cut.

Deaf saw the bomb and spoke the info aloud, which Blind and I both heard - great, that solves the communication problem more directly than I expected. Light is blue, so per the manual, cut wire color = blue. Looking at the wires in order: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Blue is wire position 5.

Now I need to get "cut wire 5" to Blind. But I can't speak - only gesture, and only Deaf can see gestures. Blind cannot see gestures at all. So I still cannot reach Blind directly.

However, Deaf can hear... wait, Deaf cannot hear anything (Deaf's restriction is "cannot hear anything, or touch the bomb"). So Deaf cannot hear Blind or me either. Deaf only sees.

So the only way to relay to Blind is through gestures to Deaf, but Deaf can't speak to Blind... wait Deaf CAN speak (Deaf's cannot list is hear/touch, not speak). Deaf spoke already. So Deaf can speak to Blind.

So: I gesture the wire number to Deaf, Deaf speaks it to Blind.

I'll gesture the number 5 using a clear symbol convention. Let me use finger-count style gestures: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🖐=3... Actually let me just use a simple numeric gesture code I define: I'll send five distinct gestures where position corresponds to count, using ☝ repeated, or just pick single symbols for numbers 1-5.

Simplest: 👆 = "this many" counting gesture. I'll send ☝ five times isn't ideal since deaf needs to know it means "cut wire number 5" not "wire 1 five times".

I'll use: 🫱 to mean "cut wire number:" marker, then five ✌ style... Let's just directly send five instances of a chosen symbol representing count.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

Deaf gestured back a single 👍 to me - likely acknowledging receipt, but I intended to send five ☝ symbols to represent "wire number 5". It seems only one symbol registered, or Deaf is just confirming they saw something and is now translating.

Wait, looking again - my turn 2 message was `gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])` — that should have sent 6 symbols total (👍 followed by five ☝). Deaf's response shows only "[👍]" which might just be an acknowledgment gesture back to me, not a report of what they received. I can't be sure they got the full count.

I should wait now and see if Deaf successfully spoke the instruction to Blind (since Deaf can speak). If Blind reports back with something wrong, I'll need to correct via gesture. For now, there's nothing more productive to send - let me wait and check the next arrivals to confirm Blind got "cut wire 5".

Let me reconsider: Deaf received "[👍]" only shown to me, meaning Deaf saw just one symbol clearly, or the counting gestures got confused.

Deaf clarified something important: I actually CAN hear Deaf's speech (Mute's restriction is "cannot speak", not "cannot hear"). So Deaf's spoken words reach me. That means Deaf can directly tell Blind the answer too, and I just need to confirm what to cut.

Let me gesture clearly again, explaining with simple symbols that 🖖 = 5, and confirm the instruction directly, since Deaf can now correlate light=blue with my earlier table gesture (👍=blue, first pair 👍👍ent meant blue→blue).

I'll resend clearly with a simpler approach: gesture the wire position count using distinct taps.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🖖"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Blind waiting for cut instruction. Board: display 0, light blue, wires 1 white 2 red 3 green 4 yellow 5 blue.

Deaf wants me to gesture one symbol per wire color in the manual's order, so they can match colors to positions using what they see. Let me re-send my table clearly as light-color paired with cut-color, one pair at a time, using distinct symbols per color so Deaf can build a personal code:

blue=👍, green=👎, red=👌, white=☝, yellow=✌

Table rows (light, cut-color):
1. blue, blue → 👍 👍
2. green, white → 👎 ☝
3. red, yellow → 👌 ✌
4. white, red → ☝ 👌
5. yellow, green → ✌ 👎

This is exactly what I sent in Turn 1. Deaf may not have caught it since it was before Deaf explained they need a code established first. Let me resend this pairing, and also explicitly note (via gesture ordering) that first symbol = light color, second = wire-to-cut color, so Deaf can see the light is blue, match to first pair, and see the cut color is blue too - then find blue in the wire list (position 5) and tell Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "✌"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: I see the same five pairs again: thumbsup thumbsup, thumbsdown index, ok peace, index ok, peace thumbsdown. Are these one pair per wire, in the order white red green yellow blue? If so what do the symbols mean - please assign each symbol a number 1 to 5 by repeating that symbol that many times so I can learn the code.
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Deaf relayed your gestures as pairs per wire: white=thumbsup-thumbsup, red=thumbsdown-index, green=ok-peace, yellow=index-ok, blue=peace-thumbsdown. I don't know your symbol meanings. Can you gesture a single symbol per wire meaning CUT or SAFE, one at a time, so Deaf can relay unambiguously? Or gesture just the position number of the wire to cut using that many repeats of one symbol like thumbsup?

Both Deaf and Blind now suggest the same clean solution: gesture the wire position number using repeated symbols. This avoids needing any pre-shared code - they can just count. Let me do exactly that.

The light is blue → cut wire color is blue (per manual) → blue is wire position 5 (from the list: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue).

I'll gesture 👍 repeated 5 times, nothing else, so Deaf can count and relay "wire 5" to Blind unambiguously.

```

```
